claim.qualifier: Ford continues to sell remaining 2024 inventory through dealer network. Marketing site and configurator continue to operate as if the Lightning is a current product.
claim.verbatim_quote: Get behind the wheel of the all-electric Ford F-150 Lightning

reality.qualifier: Production of the 2025 Lightning has been halted per Consumer Reports' updated product page. Ford's announced next-generation Lightning will be a series-hybrid extended-range EV with an onboard generator (a fundamentally different powertrain), targeted at up to 700 mi range.
reality.verbatim_quote: Production of the 2025 Lightning has been discontinued. The next-generation Lightning will be an extended-range electric vehicle with an onboard generator, promising a range of up to 700 miles.

sources.name: Consumer Reports — Ford F-150 Lightning overview (updated)

narrative_one_liner: Ford halted 2025 Lightning production; marketing page presents it as a current product.
narrative: Ford has halted production of the 2025 F-150 Lightning. Consumer Reports' product page reflects this; Ford's own marketing site and configurator do not prominently disclose it to shoppers researching the truck. The next-generation Lightning is announced as a series-hybrid (range-extender) vehicle with an onboard generator — a fundamentally different powertrain that will not share parts, charging behavior, or warranty profile with the current battery-electric Lightning. Buyers comparing 'current' EV trucks should know they are evaluating end-of-line inventory.
methodology_notes: Single Tier-2 source (CR). Pending: locate Ford's primary disclosure (press release or 10-K mention) to elevate to Tier 1.
caveats: Ford has not, as of access date, made a prominent press-release disclosure of the production halt that we have found. Phase 1 task: search Ford investor-relations releases.
'Discontinued' may mean 'paused' rather than 'permanent'; CR's wording is unambiguous but not necessarily Ford's official position.
Single Tier-2 source — graded B until Ford official disclosure surfaces.
alternative_explanations: Production may have been paused for retooling rather than discontinued; the next-gen series-hybrid would suggest discontinuation of the current platform.
Inventory channel-stuffing late in a model's lifecycle is normal; what matters is whether Ford disclosed the change to buyers in the moment of purchase consideration.
